snippet.title: How to Make Money Clipping GTA 6 Videos (Turned Into A Free Skill)
snippet.description:
🎁 The GTA 6 Clipper (free skill) + setup: https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
🌘 FinalPhase: https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about

An AI that clips GTA 6 streams for you. Give it a stream link from YouTube, Twitch or Kick (or nothing, and it finds today's biggest GTA 6 streams), and you get ready-to-post vertical clips: facecam on top, gameplay below, a hook title, word-by-word captions and a post caption with hashtags. Everything in this video is free.

🎮 What it does, in 4 steps
1. Downloads only the audio. A 4-hour stream is a couple hundred MB, not a giant video file.
2. Listens to the whole stream on your computer: a transcript, where the streamer got loud, and (on YouTube replays) where chat suddenly sped up.
3. The AI reads the transcript 12 minutes at a time and picks what people share: first reactions, crazy discoveries, freakouts, funny fails, hot takes. Every moment gets a score, and anything that needs context gets thrown out.
4. Downloads only the minutes it needs, finds the facecam by itself and makes the clips, plus a caption and hashtags for each one.

📊 The real run in this video
TimTheTatman's GTA 6 Extended Look reaction stream: 4 h 09 min → 39 possible moments → the best 3 kept, in 13 min 48 s. It makes 3 clips per stream by default and runs several streams at once, so 7 streams ≈ 21 clips.

💳 Way 1: your Claude subscription (how every clip in this video was made)
Plans start at $20/month. No API keys. Everything except the picking runs on your computer.
1. Download the clipper from the free Skool and put it in your Claude skills folder (the Skool post has a paste-in prompt that does it for you).
2. Open Claude Code and say: set up the GTA 6 clipper. It checks what your computer needs, installs what's missing and tells you when it's ready.
3. Say: clip this stream, and paste the link. Or: find me today's biggest GTA 6 streams and clip them.

🆓 Way 2: free, no subscription, no API key
1. Install Ollama and Claude Code (both free).
2. Check your memory, not your storage: Apple menu → About This Mac → Memory.
3. 16 GB → download Qwen 3.5 9B. 32 GB or more → Qwen 3.5 27B. More memory = smarter model = better picks.
4. Open Terminal, type ollama launch claude and pick your model.
5. Same prompts as Way 1.
Honest take: the free model isn't Claude. It's slower, the picks are rougher, and expect some back and forth before you get clips you like. It still beats scrubbing a stream by hand.

⚠️ Good to know
• Mac only for now.
• Age-restricted YouTube streams (common with GTA) and Kick need your browser login: add --cookies chrome.
• Clip streamers who are fine with clipping, and watch every clip before you post it.
• YouTube ad money needs the Partner Program (1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours in 12 months, or 10M Shorts views in 90 days), and YouTube can refuse it for reposted, mass-made content. Add something of your own.

✏️ Notes on the intro
• The "2.5 million people / £400 million" figures come from Uswitch: a survey of 1,000 UK workers who play games, scaled up to about 2.56 million UK workers taking 19 November off, ≈ £403.5 million in work hours. An estimate, not a count.
• There's no official GTA 6 budget. Most analyst estimates are $1–1.5 billion; $2 billion is the top of the guesses.
• GTA 6 comes out 19 November 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, 13 years after GTA 5 (2013).

snippet.title: How To Create GTA 6 Clips With AI (FREE SKILL)
snippet.description:
🚀 Final Phase (the video editors and caption styles, all 23 of our skills in 1 platform): https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
I built a clipper that turns a GTA 6 stream into vertical clips that are ready to post, and on launch day it can clip a stream while it's still live.

🆓 Our free Skool (the clipper, over 50 packs from my videos, over 23,000 people): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Already in Final Phase? The editors are already in the platform.
Weekly calls if you get stuck installing anything.

The real run: three GTA 6 Extended Look reaction streams at once, from CaseOh, MoistCr1TiKaL and Jynxzi. That's five and a half hours of stream. It listened to all of it in about eight minutes, found 34 moments worth a look and kept nine, three per stream. From pasting three links to nine clips ready to post took about 30 minutes, and I didn't touch anything in between.

What the clipper does
1. You give it a link from YouTube, Twitch or Kick, or it finds today's biggest GTA 6 streams by itself.
2. It downloads only the audio (a four-hour stream is a few hundred megabytes) and transcribes it on your computer, marking where the streamer laughed, screamed or got louder than their normal.
3. It reads the room: how fast chat moves compared to normal, what chat types ("CLIP IT", "LMAO", walls of question marks), YouTube's most-replayed graph, and the clips Twitch viewers already made, down to the second. All of it goes into one hype curve.
4. The AI reads the transcript 12 minutes at a time and scores every moment, harshly. The best ones go head to head in a final round: would a stranger stop scrolling in two seconds, does it make sense with zero context, does it pay off inside the clip.
5. It never clips the same moment twice, and it warns you when there's a copyrighted song under a clip.
6. It downloads only the minutes it needs, finds the facecam, picks the layout scene by scene, cuts the dead air, adds a hook title and word-by-word captions and sets the volume where Shorts want it.
7. Every clip checks itself (length, loudness, black frames, the face), gets a caption with hashtags, and lands on a page where you can watch them all and copy each caption.

Live mode: say "clip this live stream" and paste the link. It records in the background, listens every 20 seconds, and when chat explodes it shows Claude the last minute. A yes is a finished clip on your computer about three minutes after it happened.

Two ways to run it
Way 1: your Claude subscription (Pro is $20 a month billed monthly, or $17 a month billed yearly, US prices on claude.com/pricing). Everything except the picking runs on your computer for free, no API keys. Put the clipper in your Claude skills folder (or drag the folder into Claude Code) and say "set up the clipper".
Way 2: free. Install Ollama and Claude Code, download a model that fits your memory (16 GB: Qwen 3.5 9B, 32 GB or more: Qwen 3.5 27B), then run "ollama launch claude". The free model is slower and its picks are rougher; everything else runs the same.

Before you post
YouTube pays Shorts through the YouTube Partner Program: 1,000 subscribers and 10 million valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days. It can turn down channels that only repost, so add something of your own. Clip streamers who are fine with clipping, and watch every clip before you post it.

Credits
Stream footage shown for commentary: MoreCaseOh, MoistCr1TiKaL Gaming and Jynxzi on YouTube. The GTA VI trailer playing inside their streams belongs to Rockstar Games. Real chat replay from MoistCr1TiKaL Gaming's stream. The crowd-clip example uses clips viewers made of TimTheTatman's Twitch VOD. Pages shown: skool.com, contentrewards.com, claude.com, ollama.com, support.google.com. Not affiliated with any of them. This video is not sponsored.

snippet.title: Make Money Clipping GTA 6 Videos (Turned Into A Free Skill)
snippet.description:
Skill Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qDe_jqlRXwaF7N0rFOP-9SpgT4mw84fo?usp=sharing

🎮 Turn GTA 6 Streams Into Viral Shorts Using AI (100% Free Setup!)

What if you could turn a 4-hour GTA 6 livestream into multiple ready-to-post YouTube Shorts without watching the entire stream?

That's exactly what this AI-powered GTA 6 Clipper does.

Just paste a YouTube, Twitch, or Kick stream link — or let the AI discover the biggest GTA 6 livestreams happening today. It automatically finds the most exciting moments and turns them into vertical videos with facecam, gameplay, animated captions, catchy hooks, and social media descriptions.

And the best part? You can build this entire workflow for free!

🚀 How This AI GTA 6 Clipper Works

The system follows 4 simple steps:

1. Downloads Stream Audio

Instead of downloading an entire 4-hour livestream, it extracts only the audio, saving time and storage.

2. Analyses the Entire Stream

AI processes the audio locally and identifies:
- Full video transcripts
- Exciting or loud reactions
- Funny moments and unexpected discoveries
- Chat activity spikes on YouTube replays

3. Finds the Most Viral Moments

AI analyses the transcript in 12-minute sections and looks for moments people would actually want to share.

It identifies:
- First reactions
- Crazy GTA 6 discoveries
- Funny fails
- Streamer freakouts
- Unexpected moments
- Interesting opinions and hot takes

Every moment gets a score, and clips that need too much context are automatically rejected.

4. Automatically Creates Shorts

The system downloads only the relevant video sections and creates:
- Vertical 9:16 videos
- Facecam on top
- GTA 6 gameplay below
- Hook-based titles
- Word-by-word captions
- Social media descriptions
- Relevant hashtags

Here's what happened when I tested it on a real livestream:

- Stream duration: 30 minutes
- Potential moments discovered: 15
- Best moments selected: 3
- Processing time: 13 minutes 48 seconds

By default, it generates 3 clips per stream.

You can also process multiple livestreams simultaneously. For example, 7 streams could generate approximately 21 clips.

💳 METHOD 1: Use Your Claude Subscription

This is the method used to create all the clips in this demonstration.

Requirements:
- Claude subscription (plans start at $20/month)
- Claude Code
- GTA 6 Clipper files

Setup:

1. Download the free GTA 6 Clipper from the Skool community.
2. Move the downloaded files into your Claude skills folder.
3. Open Claude Code.
4. Type: `Set up the GTA 6 clipper`
5. Let Claude check your computer, install dependencies, and configure everything.

Once setup is complete, simply type:

`Clip this stream: [PASTE STREAM LINK]`

Or let AI find streams automatically:

`Find today's biggest GTA 6 streams and clip them.`

No separate API keys required. Most processing happens locally on your computer.

## 🆓 METHOD 2: Completely Free — No Claude Subscription

Want to build this without paying for Claude?

You can use Ollama with a locally running Qwen model.

Requirements:
- Ollama
- Claude Code
- A compatible computer

Recommended models:
- 16 GB RAM → Qwen 3.5 9B
- 32 GB RAM or more → Qwen 3.5 27B

Setup:

1. Install Ollama.
2. Install Claude Code.
3. Download the recommended Qwen model.
4. Open Terminal.
5. Run: `ollama launch claude`
6. Select your downloaded model.
7. Open Claude Code and use the same clipping prompts.

Honest comparison:

The free local model isn't as capable as Claude. Expect slower processing, less accurate clip selection, and some trial and error.

But it can still save you hours of manually searching through livestreams.

⚠️ Important Things You Should Know

- Currently supports Mac only.
- Age-restricted YouTube streams and Kick may require browser authentication using `--cookies chrome`.
- Only clip streamers who permit clipping.
- Always review your clips before publishing.
- YouTube monetization isn't guaranteed for AI-generated or reused clips.

For YouTube ad revenue, you generally need to qualify for the YouTube Partner Program: 1,000 subscribers and 4,000 valid public watch hours in 12 months, or 10 million valid public Shorts views in 90 days.

Simply reposting livestream clips at scale may not qualify for monetization. Add original commentary, editing, analysis, or meaningful creative value.

 Who Can Use This?

- GTA 6 content creators
- YouTube Shorts creators
- Gaming clip channels
- Twitch and Kick stream editors
- Content agencies
- Anyone looking to automate video clipping

The bigger idea isn't just GTA 6. It's using AI to turn long-form content into short-form content automatically.

---

Disclaimer:
This video is for educational purposes. Respect creators' copyright, platform policies, and clipping permissions before downloading or publishing livestream content.
